_comment: ACTUAL cost, as billed. Everything the dashboard computes itself is an ESTIMATE derived from Batch job start/stop times. This file holds real, invoiced figures, and it is edited by a person because no automation on this account can fetch one.
_why_a_file_and_not_an_api: This AWS account (073795725844) is denied every cost API by an explicit Deny in service control policy p-q1ngvul9 on organisation o-z3xgjt2s3d - Cost Explorer, Budgets, Cost and Usage Reports and the Free Tier API alike. The organisation's management account is 897729121516 (aws-master+ucsd3@strategic-blue.com): this is a CloudBank-funded account billed through Strategic Blue. The denial is deliberate, not a misconfiguration to work around - CloudBank bills at its own rate, so AWS-side figures would not be what the grant is charged anyway.
_where_to_get_the_number: The CloudBank portal (https://www.cloudbank.org) - sign in and export the daily breakdown.
The monthly CloudBank/Strategic Blue invoice email.
Ask the UW research computing contact who administers the CloudBank allocation.
_daily_note: Daily billed totals for the whole ACCOUNT, from the CloudBank breakdown export of 2026-09-07. The account is shared - a t2.large has run continuously since 2025 and a g6e.8xlarge GPU instance ran 2026-09-05..07 - so an account total is not a campaign total. See baseline_per_day and the exclusions below.
_baseline_note: Median billed day over 2026-08-08..08-30, before the campaign started. This is standing account cost - the always-on t2.large, stored snapshots, existing S3 - and is not attributable to QuakeScope.
_exclusions_note: Billed in the campaign window but demonstrably not the campaign. Measured from CloudWatch: the g6e.8xlarge ran 9.8 h on 09-05 and 1.8 h on 09-06 at the $4.5296/h on-demand rate, and it is not on either Batch queue.

exclusions.evidence: AWS/EC2 CPUUtilization datapoints; not a Batch job

entries.note: Account billed over the campaign window ($3,124.19), less standing baseline ($96.02), less the g6e.8xlarge GPU that is not ours ($52.46), less the unattributed 2026-08-31 residual ($519.41). Gross over baseline was $3,028.16.

_calibration_note: Only days with real load calibrate the rate. 2026-08-31 is excluded: it bills $608.87 over baseline against 2,836 vCPU-hours of our compute, which is 432% of Fargate on-demand LIST price and therefore cannot be our compute at any Spot rate. Every measurable service was checked for it - no NAT gateway exists, no EC2 ran that day but the always-on t2.large (including instances since terminated, checked via CloudWatch rather than describe-instances), DocumentDB was one idle t4g.medium, log ingestion was $0.79, S3 storage was under a gigabyte. Nothing found. Being the last day of the month it most likely carries August's monthly-posted charges, but one month of data cannot prove that, so it is recorded as unattributed rather than assigned to the campaign. Including it inflated the rate by 21% and made Fargate Spot look far more expensive than it is.

unattributed.why: billed over baseline, less what our 2,836 vCPU-h are worth at the September rate ($89.46). Not attributed to any service.
